t658.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Burayd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Burda al-Ash'ari al-Kufi as trustworthy who errs a little, of the sixth generation.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة. وكذلك قال أحمد بن عبد الله العجلي
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
He is not firm, and his hadith can be written down.
عمرو بن علي, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم أسمع يحيى ولا عبد الرحمن يحدثان عن سفيان عنه بشيء قط
I never heard Yaḥyā or ʿAbd al-Raḥmān transmit anything from Sufyān through him.
روى عنه الأئمة والثقات، ولم يرو عنه أحد أكثر مما رواه أبو أسامة، وأحاديثه عنه مستقيمة، وهو صدوق
Leading scholars and reliable transmitters reported from him. Abū Usāmah transmitted the most from him, and Abū Usāmah’s reports from him are sound. Burayd was truthful.
وهذا طريق حسن، رواه ثقات، وقد أدخله قوم في صحاحهم، وأرجو أن لا يكون به بأس
This is a good chain through reliable transmitters. Some included it in their Ṣaḥīḥ collections, and I hope there is no problem with it.

t7507.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn Aktham ibn Muḥammad ibn Qaṭan al-Tamīmī al-Marwazī, known as Abū Muḥammad, the famous judge, a jurist, truthful, though accused of stealing hadith, which did not occur from him; rather it was transmission by ijāza and wijāda. Of the tenth generation, he died at the end of 242 or 243 AH at the age of eighty-three.
as: فقيه صدوق إلا أنه رمي بسرقة الحديث ولم يقع ذلك له وإنما كان هى الرواية بالإجازة والوجادة
A jurist, truthful, except that he was accused of stealing hadith, but that did not occur from him; rather it was transmission by license (ijāza) and finding (wijāda).
